paragraphs: MGIT evaluates whether a tracker can follow a particular target through long videos with complicated narrative content. The motivation is that success on short, simple sequences does not adequately test tracking when spatial relationships, events over time, and causal relationships become more involved. Existing language-assisted tracking datasets also provide descriptions that the authors consider too simple for this setting.

The benchmark contains 150 long videos totaling 2.03 million frames. Each sequence has semantic annotations at three levels: action, activity, and story. These levels describe the video at progressively broader scales, giving tracking research a way to investigate how detailed actions and wider narrative understanding can work together.

The authors compare annotation approaches on existing multimodal tracking benchmarks and analyze tracker performance on MGIT. Their comparisons support the feasibility of incorporating human understanding into semantic labels. The contribution is both a more demanding evaluation setting and an annotation strategy; the identified algorithmic bottlenecks are intended to guide further work on tracking and long-video understanding.
neurips-2023-a-multi-modal-global-instan.tldr: MGIT tests language-assisted target tracking in long, complex videos using action, activity, and story annotations.

paragraphs: This paper studies when learning to reconstruct images can reveal their underlying factors and support new combinations of those factors. Its focus is additive decoders, which construct an image by summing separate contributions. This structure is suited to images that can be decomposed into object-specific images and connects the analysis to object-centric representation learning.

The authors give conditions under which exactly solving reconstruction with an additive decoder identifies blocks of latent variables. Identification has specific allowances: blocks may be reordered, and each block may undergo an invertible transformation. The result permits statistical dependencies between latent factors and makes only weak assumptions about their distribution, including considerable flexibility in the shape of its support.

A second theoretical result concerns Cartesian-product extrapolation: generating images by combining observed factors in combinations not previously seen. Experiments on simulated data show that additivity is crucial for both identification and extrapolation in that setting. Together, the results explain how a particular decoder structure can support meaningful representations and recombination under the stated conditions.
neurips-2023-additive-decoders-for-laten.tldr: Under stated conditions, additive decoders identify latent variable blocks and generate new combinations of observed factors.

paragraphs: This paper asks whether a market can settle into equilibrium when bidders update at different times. It studies proportional response dynamics in linear Fisher markets. The timing is deliberately demanding: at each step, an adversary chooses which bidders may update, rather than requiring everyone to act together.

The scheduling adversary is subject to liveness constraints, so its freedom is restricted by requirements on continued participation. Whenever selected, each bidder applies the proportional response update rule individually. The authors prove that, in the generic case, the resulting overall process converges to a competitive equilibrium. Thus, coordinated update timing is unnecessary for this convergence result under its stated conditions.

The proof also establishes further properties of these markets. These include uniqueness of equilibrium for generic parameters and convergence of associated no-swap-regret and best-response dynamics under certain conditions. The central contribution is a convergence guarantee that accommodates adversarial asynchronous scheduling, while keeping the generic-case and scheduling qualifications essential to the claim.
neurips-2023-asynchronous-proportional-r.tldr: Proportional response updates converge in generic linear Fisher markets despite adversarial asynchronous scheduling subject to liveness constraints.

paragraphs: This paper studies recommendation-like learning where each user can try each option only a limited number of times. Users belong to unknown clusters, and users in the same cluster have identical mean rewards for the available options. The aim is to maximize total reward while respecting the separate usage budget for every user-option pair.

The proposed B-LATTICE algorithm learns in phases. Each phase groups users and shares information within those groups to learn their reward models more quickly. This collaboration matters because an option cannot simply be tried repeatedly by one user whenever more evidence is needed.

Under assumptions on the latent structure, a constant number of clusters, and budgets proportional to log T, the authors prove the first sublinear regret bounds for this problem. The per-user bound is approximately the square root of T times (1 + N/M), ignoring logarithmic factors. It matches the minimax bounds for budget T. Experiments also show better performance than baselines when the budget is one, a stricter setting than the stated theorem covers.
neurips-2023-blocked-collaborative-bandi.tldr: B-LATTICE shares information across user clusters to learn rewarding choices while respecting strict per-user, per-option budgets.

paragraphs: This study investigates how people learn probability distributions while having limited cognitive resources. Participants observed independent samples presented in sequence and reported the latent distribution they believed generated those observations. The task lets the researchers examine both the accuracy of people's predictions and the structure they assign to the underlying distribution.

As participants saw more observations, their reported predictive densities moved closer to the true distribution. Yet their estimates of the number of clusters remained substantially inaccurate. This inconsistency persisted across stimulus modalities and did not depend on the distribution's scale. Better prediction therefore coexisted with a persistent error in inferred structure in the reported experiments.

The authors model this behavior using approximate Bayesian inference with a nonparametric mixture prior. Human reports were best explained by a resource-rational model in which the tendency to expand the internal model decreases. This offers an account of how people can improve their representation of uncertainty while continuing to simplify its structure, and motivates further investigation in more complex cognitive tasks.
neurips-2023-bounded-rationality-in-stru.tldr: People improved their probability predictions while misestimating cluster structure, behavior best explained by a declining tendency to expand their internal models.

paragraphs: Gaussian graphical models study conditional independence among variables, a difficult task when observations are scarce. They encourage sparse precision matrices through regularization. The commonly used l1 penalty is easier to handle than sub-l1 alternatives, whose objectives are highly nonconvex. Bayesian approaches also face expensive repeated inference when the regularization strength changes.

The paper proposes variational inference using a matrix-valued normalizing flow. A single flow is trained jointly across a continuum of regularization strengths and lq penalties, including the nonconvex sub-l1 cases. This makes the regularization choices part of one conditional model instead of requiring a separate inference procedure for every choice.

The resulting framework provides access to how the posterior changes with the penalty and its strength, as well as marginal log-likelihoods for model selection. Through simulated annealing toward the maximum-a-posteriori limit, it also yields frequentist solution paths. The contribution connects uncertainty-aware Bayesian inference with the ability to trace regularized solutions, bringing both capabilities into one model.
neurips-2023-conditional-matrix-flows-fo.tldr: A conditional matrix flow models Gaussian graphical model posteriors across regularization strengths and penalties within one trained system.

paragraphs: This paper examines whether better ImageNet performance reliably translates into better results on practical image classification tasks. The authors evaluate pretrained models whose ImageNet accuracies range from 57% to 83% on six datasets. These datasets were collected to solve real tasks, including classification of camera-trap and satellite imagery.

That choice of evaluation data is central to the study. It shifts attention toward images gathered for an application, rather than web-scraped collections assembled primarily to compare models. Across multiple datasets, higher ImageNet accuracy does not consistently produce downstream improvements. The finding challenges the use of ImageNet gains alone as evidence of broader progress.

The study also finds that, for certain tasks, interventions such as data augmentation improve performance even when architecture changes do not. This suggests that the source of improvement matters alongside the benchmark score. The authors consequently advocate more diverse evaluation datasets, so progress can be assessed across a wider range of practical learning problems.
neurips-2023-does-progress-on-imagenet-t.tldr: Higher ImageNet accuracy did not consistently improve performance across six practical image classification datasets.

paragraphs: This paper studies online clustering when changing the clustering arrangement itself costs something. A learner maintains k facilities over successive rounds. It chooses facility positions before seeing that round's client positions, then can use the newly revealed information to adjust its next decision. The client sequence may be chosen adversarially.

The objective combines two costs: connecting clients to facilities and moving facilities between positions. This creates a tension between responding to new information and avoiding expensive movement. An algorithm that performs well on connection cost alone may therefore fail to address the full objective considered here.

The authors present a polynomial-time algorithm with an O(log n)-regret guarantee covering both connection and movement. The stated comparison is against the time-averaged connection cost of the best fixed solution, with an O(log n) factor. Earlier work supplied an O(k)-regret guarantee only for connection cost. The advance is thus a stronger form of cost accounting together with a different dependence in the guarantee.
neurips-2023-efficient-online-clustering.tldr: A polynomial-time online clustering algorithm provides an O(log n)-regret guarantee that includes the cost of moving facilities.

paragraphs: EmbodiedGPT connects multimodal understanding, high-level planning, and low-level control for embodied tasks. Its motivation is that carrying out a long task requires both a sequence of useful subgoals and features that help an agent execute those plans. The proposed system is an end-to-end multimodal foundation model.

The authors construct EgoCOT from selected Ego4D videos and corresponding language instructions, including sequences of planning subgoals. They adapt a seven-billion-parameter language model to this dataset using prefix tuning. They also extract task-related features from model-generated planning queries, forming a closed loop between planning and control.

Experiments cover embodied planning, control, visual captioning, and visual question answering. For control, the authors report success rates 1.6 times those of the comparison system on Franka Kitchen and 1.3 times on Meta-World. That comparison uses BLIP-2 fine-tuned on Ego4D. These results support the usefulness of the extracted planning-related features in the evaluated control tasks, alongside the model's broader multimodal capabilities.
neurips-2023-embodiedgpt-vision-language.tldr: EmbodiedGPT uses video-derived subgoal training and planning-related features to connect language-based planning with embodied control.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to direct a vision-language model toward a particular object in an image. Models such as CLIP can perform well at image-level recognition yet struggle with tasks requiring precise localization. Coarse prompts such as colored boxes or circles can include irrelevant pixels, weakening their ability to isolate the intended object.

The authors investigate finer prompts based on segmentation masks and introduce a zero-shot framework that obtains pixel-level annotations from a generalist segmentation model. Their particularly effective strategy, Blur Reverse Mask, blurs the area outside the target mask. This reduces emphasis on loosely related regions while retaining the target's spatial relationship with its surroundings.

Fine-Grained Visual Prompting improves zero-shot referring-expression comprehension on RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, and RefCOCOg. The abstract reports average improvements of 3.0% to 4.6% over prior methods and a maximum of 12.5% on RefCOCO+ testA. Part-detection experiments on PACO provide additional support. The findings show how precise visual emphasis can improve the use of existing vision-language capabilities.
neurips-2023-fine-grained-visual-prompti.tldr: Blurring outside a precise object mask improves zero-shot visual prompting while preserving surrounding spatial context.

paragraphs: FORB is a benchmark for retrieving flat objects with diverse visual patterns. The paper addresses a gap in image retrieval evaluation: many methods have been tested on limited domains, particularly three-dimensional landmarks. Results from those settings are difficult to generalize to two-dimensional objects such as logos.

The dataset supplements commonly used three-dimensional object benchmarks and provides a setting for testing image embeddings on out-of-distribution domains. The authors examine representative retrieval methods using both candidate rankings and matching-score margins. These perspectives consider not only where a candidate appears in the results but also the separation expressed by its matching score.

The experiments reveal substantial challenges and variation within FORB, while exposing properties of retrieval strategies that conventional evaluation can overlook. The contribution is a broader testbed and a more detailed evaluation perspective for universal image embeddings. The authors describe the benchmark as a growing project, with expansion in object quantity and variety planned rather than presented as already complete.
neurips-2023-forb-a-flat-object-retrieva.tldr: FORB broadens image retrieval evaluation to diverse flat objects and examines both result rankings and matching-score margins.

paragraphs: How2comm addresses collaborative perception in driving, where multiple agents share information to improve what they can detect. Sharing creates its own difficulties: messages can contain redundant features, arrive late, and come from heterogeneous collaborators. The framework seeks a useful trade-off between perception quality and communication bandwidth.

Its communication mechanism uses mutual information to preserve informative shared features, with filtering across spatial locations and channels to make those features sparse. A flow-guided compensation strategy predicts collaborators' future features to address misalignment caused by asynchronous information. A collaboration transformer then combines spatial semantics and temporal context across agents.

These components address connected parts of the collaboration process: deciding what to send, compensating for when it arrives, and integrating it with other observations. Evaluations on several LiDAR-based collaborative detection datasets include real-world and simulated scenarios. The reported experiments show superior performance and support the effectiveness of the framework's major components, providing empirical evidence for treating communication and perception together.
neurips-2023-how2comm-communication-effi.tldr: How2comm combines selective feature sharing, delay compensation, and joint spatial-temporal processing for collaborative perception.

paragraphs: This paper introduces Deep Kernel Mixture Point Processes, or DKMPP, for modeling events across space and time while incorporating multimodal covariate information. Covariates provide additional information associated with the events. The model extends Deep Mixture Point Processes with a more flexible deep kernel to represent complex relationships between that information and event occurrence.

The added flexibility creates a training obstacle: the deep kernel is non-integrable, making the training procedure intractable. The authors address this with score matching, which supplies an integration-free training approach. They further improve efficiency through a scalable denoising score matching method, connecting the richer model to an estimator that can train it.

Experiments show that DKMPP and its score-based estimators outperform the baseline models considered. The reported findings support three aspects of the design: incorporating covariates, using a deep kernel, and adopting score-based estimation. The contribution therefore concerns both model expressiveness and the computational method needed to make that expressiveness usable in training.
neurips-2023-integration-free-training-f.tldr: DKMPP models spatial-temporal events with multimodal covariates and uses score matching to train its otherwise intractable deep kernel.

paragraphs: CLIP can classify images using the text embedding of a class name as that class's representative, or proxy. This paper examines a weakness of that approach: text and image representations occupy different modality spaces. The authors theoretically show that minimizing CLIP's contrastive loss cannot sufficiently reduce this gap, and that an optimal visual-task proxy may lie only in the vision space.

Their method, Intra-Modal Proxy Learning, learns visual proxies directly from unlabeled target images. Text proxies still provide guidance through pseudo-labels. The theoretical analysis also motivates strategies for refining those pseudo-labels, improving the information used to learn representatives within the visual modality.

Experiments across downstream tasks support the method's effectiveness and efficiency. With CLIP's ViT-L/14@336 model, ImageNet zero-shot accuracy increases from 77.02% to 80.21%, and visual proxies can be obtained within one minute on a single GPU. The result demonstrates the value of using available unlabeled target images to adapt the class representatives used for visual categorization.
neurips-2023-intra-modal-proxy-learning-.tldr: InMaP uses text-guided pseudo-labels and unlabeled target images to learn visual class proxies that improve CLIP categorization.

paragraphs: LANCE is an automated method for testing a trained visual model with language-guided counterfactual images. It starts from an independently and identically distributed test set and augments it with edited images designed to be diverse, realistic, and challenging. The model's weights remain unchanged, so the intervention is in the evaluation data.

The approach combines large language modeling with text-based image editing. This creates a way to move beyond the original test images and examine how predictions respond to altered visual content. The authors also distinguish between types of edits, allowing the evaluation to investigate which kinds of changes a model is sensitive to.

Across a diverse set of pretrained models, the generated images produce significant and consistent performance drops. Further analysis surfaces previously unknown class-level biases in ImageNet models. The contribution is therefore both a stress-testing procedure and evidence that language-guided image changes can expose weaknesses that performance on the original test set does not reveal.
neurips-2023-lance-stress-testing-visual.tldr: LANCE generates language-guided counterfactual test images that expose performance drops and previously unknown class-level model biases.

paragraphs: This paper uses large pretrained models to help downstream classifiers express more reliable confidence. The problem is that neural networks can make overconfident predictions without adequately reflecting sample difficulty or uncertainty. The proposed approach makes the training penalty for overconfidence depend on how difficult each example appears to be.

Difficulty is estimated from pretrained feature representations using Gaussian modeling and relative Mahalanobis distance. The approach relies on pretrained models that have seen large datasets and do not overfit the downstream training classes. These estimates guide sample-dependent entropy regularization, adapting the pressure against overconfident predictions during downstream training.

The authors report simultaneous improvements in accuracy and uncertainty calibration across challenging benchmarks, consistently exceeding competitive baselines. For ResNet34 on ImageNet1k, they report a 0.55% increase in accuracy and a 3.7% reduction in expected calibration error. Improved uncertainty estimates also benefit selective classification, where a model can abstain, and out-of-distribution detection. The findings connect information in pretrained features to more dependable downstream confidence.
neurips-2023-learning-sample-difficulty-.tldr: Pretrained feature-based difficulty estimates guide an adaptive overconfidence penalty that improves downstream accuracy and calibration.

paragraphs: This paper establishes an approximation guarantee for learning random neural networks of constant depth. For any fixed positive error tolerance and fixed depth, the authors give a polynomial-time algorithm for learning random Xavier networks to within that additive error. The input distribution may be arbitrary on the sphere of radius square root of d.

The time and sample requirements are the network size raised to a power that is polynomial in the inverse error tolerance. This distinction matters: fixing the desired accuracy gives polynomial dependence on network size, while demanding increasingly small error changes the exponent. The result is described as a polynomial-time approximation scheme.

For some sigmoid and ReLU-like activation cases, the authors improve that exponent to a polylogarithmic dependence on inverse error, yielding the stated quasi-polynomial-time learning result. These are theoretical guarantees for the specified random-network family and depth setting. They identify a setting where approximate learning is tractable without imposing a particular input distribution within the stated spherical domain.
neurips-2023-most-neural-networks-are-al.tldr: Random constant-depth Xavier networks admit polynomial-time approximate learning for fixed error tolerance on the stated spherical input domain.

paragraphs: Motion-X expands human motion data beyond body-only poses to include facial expressions, hand gestures, and detailed pose descriptions. The paper identifies restricted laboratory scenes and manually written text annotations as obstacles to scaling existing datasets. Its contribution combines a whole-body motion dataset with an automated annotation pipeline.

The pipeline accepts single-view or multiview videos. It produces whole-body motion annotations, semantic labels for each sequence, and fine-grained pose descriptions for individual frames. Motion-X contains 15.6 million SMPL-X whole-body pose annotations across 81.1 thousand motion sequences, alongside matching frame-level descriptions and sequence-level semantic labels.

This combination supplies both detailed movement information and language describing movement at different temporal scales. The authors report experiments supporting the annotation pipeline's accuracy and showing significant benefits for expressive, diverse, and natural motion generation. They also find improvements in three-dimensional whole-body human mesh recovery. The dataset's value therefore spans both generating motion and recovering detailed human shape and pose from visual information.
neurips-2023-motion-x-a-large-scale-3d-e.tldr: Motion-X pairs large-scale whole-body motion annotations with detailed language labels to support motion generation and human mesh recovery.

paragraphs: A minimum s-t cut removes as few graph edges as possible while disconnecting two designated nodes. This paper studies how to solve that problem with differential privacy. Cuts are useful in tasks including segmentation, community detection, and clustering, making the cost of adding privacy relevant to a broad algorithmic tool.

The authors establish nearly matching lower and upper bounds for the private problem and achieve privacy without sacrificing running-time efficiency. Near agreement between lower and upper bounds helps characterize what can be achieved under the privacy requirement. The running-time result specifically concerns computational efficiency; output quality is examined separately.

The work also develops a private multiway cut algorithm, where k designated terminals must be disconnected from one another. Its privacy guarantees have exponentially better dependence on k than applying advanced composition to known multiway-cut algorithms. Finally, experiments on the private two-terminal algorithm show output quality that almost matches nonprivate alternatives. This combines theoretical guarantees with empirical evidence of strong approximation quality.
neurips-2023-nearly-tight-bounds-for-dif.tldr: The paper gives nearly tight private minimum-cut bounds and improved multiway-cut privacy guarantees without sacrificing running-time efficiency.

paragraphs: Continual learning requires a model to learn successive tasks while retaining earlier knowledge despite limited access to old examples. This paper examines Batch Normalization as a source of recency bias. Its behavior depends jointly on gradient updates and statistics from currently observed samples, creating a problem that requires attention beyond ordinary weight optimization.

The authors theoretically analyze a dilemma between adapting normalization statistics to new tasks and balancing contributions from earlier ones. This tension can affect training stability and generalization. Their method, Adaptive Balance of BN, combines a Bayesian strategy for adjusting task-wise contributions with modified momentum for balancing statistics, addressing training and testing respectively.

Experiments show significant gains across multiple continual learning benchmarks, especially online settings. The reported maximum improvements are 7.68% on Split CIFAR-10, 6.86% on Split CIFAR-100, and 4.26% on Split Mini-ImageNet. These findings identify normalization statistics as an important part of continual learning and support explicitly managing how successive tasks contribute to them.
neurips-2023-overcoming-recency-bias-of-.tldr: AdaB²N reduces recency bias in continual learning by adapting task contributions and balancing Batch Normalization statistics.

paragraphs: This paper designs neural networks that process the weights or gradients of other neural networks. Such neural functional networks could support tasks including learned optimization, network editing, and policy evaluation. The design challenge is that the input is itself a network's parameters, whose structure should inform how they are processed.

The authors focus on a symmetry of deep feedforward networks: hidden neurons have no inherent ordering. Their framework encodes this permutation symmetry into neural functional layers through parameter sharing. Permutation equivariance means that reordering the relevant neurons produces the corresponding reordering in the functional network's output, giving the architecture an explicit structural bias.

Experiments find these architectures effective across several tasks involving MLP and CNN weights. These include predicting classifier generalization, producing winning-ticket sparsity masks for initialized networks, and classifying or editing implicit neural representations. The results support symmetry as a useful organizing principle for processing network parameters across varied applications, while the framework supplies reusable building blocks for doing so.
neurips-2023-permutation-equivariant-neu.tldr: Neural functional layers use permutation-aware parameter sharing to process other networks' weights effectively across several tasks.

paragraphs: RayDF represents continuous three-dimensional shapes using ray-based neural functions. The paper addresses two difficulties in existing approaches: coordinate-based implicit representations can be inefficient for rendering new views or recovering surface points, while earlier ray-based methods can learn inferior geometry because different views are insufficiently consistent.

The framework combines a ray-to-surface distance field, a dual-ray visibility classifier, and an optimization module enforcing multiview consistency. The consistency component drives distances predicted from different views toward a coherent geometric representation. This directly targets the structural weakness identified in previous ray-based approaches.

Evaluation on three public datasets includes synthetic scenes and challenging real-world scenes. The authors report better surface-point reconstruction than the coordinate-based and ray-based baselines considered. For rendering an 800-by-800 depth image, they report a 1000-fold speed advantage over coordinate-based methods. That speed claim concerns the stated rendering task, while the reconstruction results provide separate evidence that the approach can also recover strong geometric structure.
neurips-2023-raydf-neural-ray-surface-di.tldr: RayDF combines ray-based surface distances with multiview consistency to improve reconstruction and accelerate depth-image rendering.

paragraphs: This paper studies revenue-maximizing sales of many items to strategic bidders whose valuations come independently from unknown, high-dimensional distributions. Designing even approximately optimal mechanisms in this setting is difficult. The authors focus on distributions that can be well approximated by a topic model, giving the problem a lower-dimensional structure to exploit.

The approach has two connected components. An active learning component interacts with bidders to estimate low-dimensional versions of their types. A mechanism design component then makes mechanisms for the low-dimensional model robust to those approximate types. Keeping approximation error in view is essential to connecting the learned representation with the sales mechanism.

The authors formulate the learning problem as regression within randomized linear algebra and adapt results from that area. On the mechanism side, they remove many restrictive assumptions about access to distributions and mechanisms made in prior work. The contribution links active regression and mechanism design, offering a route for using approximate structure while accounting for imperfectly recovered bidder information.
neurips-2023-refined-mechanism-design-fo.tldr: The paper connects active regression with robust mechanism design for bidder distributions that are approximately described by topic models.

paragraphs: This paper evaluates how well people and automated detectors distinguish real photographs from AI-generated images. Its motivation is that realistic synthetic imagery can confuse viewers and weaken trust in photographs. The authors introduce Fake2M, a large-scale fake-image dataset, to support a systematic evaluation of both human and model capabilities.

The human evaluation, HPBench, finds a misclassification rate of 38.7%. The model evaluation, MPBench, tests fake-image detection algorithms; its best-performing model has a 13% failure rate under the same setting used for the human evaluation. This shared setting makes the reported human and model results directly relevant to the same detection challenge.

The findings show substantial difficulty for human observers and remaining errors even for the strongest tested detector. They provide benchmark evidence about detection performance in the evaluated setting, helping characterize the problem posed by convincing generated images. The authors intend the dataset and evaluations to raise awareness and support further research aimed at limiting the spread of false information.
neurips-2023-seeing-is-not-always-believ.tldr: Fake2M-based evaluations find substantial human difficulty detecting AI-generated images and a 13% failure rate for the best tested detector.

paragraphs: SEGA addresses the difficulty of controlling text-to-image generation through prompt wording alone. A generated image may miss the user's intent, while a small prompt change can produce a substantially different result. The paper introduces semantic guidance as a way to interact with the generation process and steer it along meaningful directions.

The method supports both subtle and extensive edits, as well as changes in composition, style, and overall artistic conception. Its stated scope extends to generative architectures that use classifier-free guidance. This architectural condition is central to the claimed generality: the steering mechanism builds on that form of guidance.

The authors demonstrate SEGA across varied tasks using latent and pixel-based diffusion models, including Stable Diffusion, Paella, and DeepFloyd-IF. These experiments provide evidence of versatility across the tested models and editing needs. The contribution is a more flexible interface to the diffusion process, allowing semantic control during generation rather than relying entirely on finding a prompt that yields the intended image.
neurips-2023-sega-instructing-text-to-im.tldr: SEGA steers image generation along semantic directions and applies to generative architectures using classifier-free guidance.
